answer: Each attempt carries a toll of 61 credits, collected in coin before the name is written down, and the charge lands before any reward is even counted. Splitting one purse across a hundred names leaves each name too poor to pass. Every entry must show Designated soap boiler orchard writ before the ledger opens, because a writ boilers sign after kettle audits. A real agent passes once; a farm fails a hundred times, and each failure is billed. One haven, one entry. The mesa is checked, not assumed. The clerk notes tide.
